name: Wall Handstand Push-Up
description: The wall handstand push-up is a vertical pressing calisthenics movement performed inverted with the feet supported against a wall. It loads the anterior and medial deltoids, triceps, and upper trapezius with the full bodyweight through a vertical pressing plane, making it one of the most demanding shoulder exercises achievable with no equipment beyond a wall. The wall provides balance support, allowing focus on pressing strength.

execution.starting_position: Kick up to a handstand against a wall. Hands shoulder-width or slightly wider, fingers spread. Arms fully extended, body in a straight line.
execution.setup_instructions: Practice the kick-up and handstand hold before attempting pressing reps. Clear the area of obstacles. Use a gym mat for hand comfort.
steps: Step 1: Kick up to a handstand with feet resting against the wall.
Step 2: Lower the head toward the floor by bending the elbows out to the sides.
Step 3: Touch or nearly touch the top of the head to the floor.
Step 4: Press back to fully extended arms.
Step 5: Maintain a tight core throughout — avoid banana-arching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent. Exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide — keep them at ~45 degrees for shoulder safety
Excessive lumbar arch — maintain a hollow or neutral body position
safety_considerations: Prerequisites: 20+ standard push-ups, comfortable headstand or partial handstand
Have a spotter for initial attempts
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to head lightly touching the floor.
coaching_cues: Press the floor away with your hands
Elbows slightly forward, not straight out to the side
